title: Expression, Isolation, and Purification of Soluble and Insoluble Biotinylated Proteins for Nerve Tissue Regeneration
protocol: Design an amino acid sequence for the target protein using the National Center for Biotechnology Information website.
Select the active region of interest for the target protein.
Add a 6X-His tag to the N-terminus for purification.
Include a Tobacco Etch Virus protease cut site for His tag removal.
Add a biotin tagged sequence at the K residue for biotinylation.
Insert a flexible hinge with gaps between sequences.
Send the complete amino acid sequence to a company for gene design and synthesis.
Subclone the optimized gene into a vector of choice using BamHI-NotI sites.
Volumetrically add ultrapure water, mix well, and autoclave.
Let bottle cool to the touch and add ampicillin at 100 µg/ml.
Spin down plasmid vector at 6,000 x g for 3 min in order to pellet, and add 10 μl of sterilized ultrapure water.
Remove 50 μl of chemically competent E. coli high transformation efficiency cells from -80 °C and place on ice for 5-10 min.
Add 1 μl of vector solution at 0.5-1 ng/50 μl cells to the 50 μl E. coli cells and place remaining plasmid in -80 °C.
Place bacteria cells containing the vector on ice for 5 min.
Heat shock cell and vector mixture for 30-45 sec in 42 °C water bath and place cells back on ice for 2 min.
Mix 250 μl of super optimal broth with catabolite repression (SOC) medium.
Shake at 250 rpm at 37°C for 30 min.
Pipette 25, 50, and 100 μl of cell solution onto separate agar plates containing ampicillin (100 µg/ml) and tetracycline (12.5 µg/ml).
Distribute solution evenly over agar plates using glass beads.
Incubate plates upside-down at 37°C for 15-18 hours.
Check for small individual bacteria colonies on plates.
Store plates upside-down at 4°C until further use.
If no colonies are present: Check the freshness and sterility of buffers and supplies.
Increase the amount of plasmid added to E. coli K12 strain.
If large colonies or overgrowth is observed, restreak a new agar plate using a sterile inoculation loop or plate cells at lower volume.
Inoculate 5 ml LB containing ampicillin (100 µg/ml) and tetracycline (12.5 µg/ml) antibiotics with a single colony of transformed E. coli cells.
Grow-up cells overnight at 37°C at 250-300 rpm.
Isolate the target vector from the overnight grow-up using a plasmid isolation kit.
Store purified plasmid at -80°C until further use.
Mix 2-5 μl of isolated plasmid at 0.5-2 ng/50 μl cells with 50 μl E. coli expression host cells.
Heat shock the cell mixture for 60-90 seconds.
Shake the solution containing SOC medium at 250 rpm for 60 minutes.
Pluck a single colony of transformed bacteria cells from the Petri dish using a sterile applicator stick and place it in a test tube with 5 ml LB broth containing ampicillin (100 µg/ml).
Incubate the test tubes overnight at 37 °C on a shaker set to 250 rpm.
The following morning, take 200 μl of the overnight culture and add it to 5 ml LB with ampicillin at 100 µg/ml.
Freeze down the remaining cells by mixing them with 250 μl of 50% glycerol (sterile) to a total volume of 750 μl, then store in -80 °C.
Obtain a scraping of frozen cells using a sterile applicator stick and inoculate LB broth containing the appropriate antibiotics for new test expression and scale-up procedures.
Place the test tube in a shaker at 250-300 rpm at 37 °C until the optical density (OD) is measured between 0.7-0.8 at an absorbance of 600 nm.
Induce cells with IPTG to achieve a final concentration of 1 mM.
Shake cells for an additional 4 hr at 37 °C at 300 rpm.
Alternatively, shake cells overnight at 18 °C at 250-300 rpm.
Take 500 μl of culture and place in a 1.5 ml tube.
Spin down the sample at 13-15 x g for 5 min.
Pour off supernatant liquid and label "Soluble."
Resuspend pellet with vortexing in 200 μl of loading dye (50 μl 2-mercaptoethanol, 950 μl Laemmli sample buffer).
Take 1,000 μl of culture and place in a 1.5 ml tube.
Spin down the sample at 13-15 x g for 5 min.
Pour off supernatant liquid and label "Insoluble."
Resuspend insoluble pellet in 200 μl Bugbuster.
Leave the resuspended pellet at room temperature for 30 min.
Spin down the sample at 13-15 x g for 5 min.
Take 50 μl of supernatant and add it to a new "Insoluble" 1.5 ml tube.
Add 50 μl of loading dye to the new sample.
Boil both soluble and insoluble samples for 5 min.
Load each sample into an electrophoresis gel with a standard ladder.
Visualize protein samples using a staining reagent according to the company’s protocol.
Determine if the protein expresses in the soluble or insoluble fractions by comparing lanes on the SDS-PAGE gel.
Compare the lanes to soluble and insoluble control lanes.
Identify a dark band around the molecular weight of the protein in the soluble or insoluble lanes.
Choose an isolation method based on whether the band is present in the soluble, insoluble fraction, or both.
If a 4 hr and overnight induction was conducted, determine which induction method has higher protein production for scale-up.
Start an overnight culture from frozen cell stock in step 4.5.
Mix 20 ml of LB and add ampicillin at a final concentration of 100 µg/ml in a sterile Erlenmeyer flask.
Transfer a scraping of transformed E. coli cells into the flask using a sterile applicator stick, then remove the applicator stick.
Plug the flask with a foam stopper or cotton and cover it with aluminum foil to maintain sterility.
Shake overnight at 250 rpm at 37 °C.
Pour overnight culture into 1.8 L of sterile growth media and add ampicillin at 100 µg/ml.
Add 6 to 8 drops of sterile antifoam 204 using a Pasteur pipette.
Place cultures in a 37 °C water bath with 0.2 mm filtered compressed air bubbling through aeration stones.
Once the OD600nm reaches 0.7-0.8, induce with IPTG (1 mM).
Allow induction to occur for either 4 hr at 37 °C or overnight at 18 °C depending on soluble/insoluble results from SDS-PAGE in step 4.9.
Spin down the cell culture in 1 L centrifuge bottles (2 bottles/culture) for 15 min at 14,000 x g at 4 °C.
Pour off supernatant and scoop bacteria pellet into two 50 ml tubes using a thin spatula.
Pellet cells again by centrifugation for a few minutes in each tube.
Store pellets in -80°C until protein isolation.
Remove transformed E. coli pellet from -80 °C freezer.
Add 20 ml Lysis/Wash Buffer to each centrifuge tube for nonnative isolation.
Vortex and shake the frozen pellet until it thaws and solubilizes into the buffer solution without any large chunks.
Incubate on nutator overnight.
Centrifuge the slurry at 20,500 x g at room temperature for 30 min.
Transfer the supernatant to a fresh tube for isolation and discard the pellet.
Add Lysis Buffer to centrifuge tube to reach a final volume of 30 ml for native isolation.
Dislodge frozen pellet by vortexing and shaking rigorously.
Wash sonicator probe with 70% ethanol at 100% amplitude for 1-2 min.
Repeat washing the sonicator probe with ultrapure water.
Sonicate bacteria pellet while on ice for 5 min (total elapsed time of 10 min).
Centrifuge the tube up and down during sonication intervals to break up the cell pellet completely.
Ensure no visible bacteria pellet remains after sonication, leaving a stringy, viscous slurry.
Clean the sonicator probe with 70% ethanol and ultrapure water between different protein isolations as well as for storage.
Centrifuge the slurry at 20,500 x g at 4 °C for 30 min.
Transfer the supernatant to a fresh tube for isolation and discard the pellet.
Add 1 ml Ni²⁺-NTA resin solution to each centrifuge tube (2 ml total per 1.8 L culture) and incubate at room temperature on nutator for at least 1 hour.
Pour the slurry into the affinity column and allow the solution to drip completely through the stopcock valve into a waste beaker.
Perform 10 washes with 10 ml of Lysis/Wash Buffer each, adding the first two washes to the centrifuge tube before pouring into the column.
Add subsequent washes directly to the column and stir the resin with a glass stirring rod after each addition.
Close the stopcock valve once the last wash has completely dripped through.
Add 15 ml of Elution Buffer and stir-up resin, allowing the solution to sit for 5 min.
Open stopcock valve and collect elution.
Repeat step using an additional 15 ml of Elution Buffer.
Incubate Ni2+-NTA resin solution at 4 °C for at least 1 hr on nutator.
Use the appropriate Wash Buffer as per Table 1.
Add 5 ml of Elution Buffer to the resin and incubate for 5 min.
Open stopcock valve and collect elution until most of the solution has dripped through.
Add 90 μl of Bradford reagent to clear 96-well plate.
After each elution, allow 10 μl of solution to drip from column into well containing 90 μl Bradford reagent.
Continue adding 5 ml Elution Buffer at a time until Bradford assay no longer detects protein (color goes from dark blue to light blue to clear).
This usually takes 4-5 elution volumes.
Make nonnative (renaturation) and native dialysis buffers as per Table 1.
Store dialysis buffers in 4 °C.
Transfer native and nonnative elutions to dialysis tubing with appropriate molecular weight cutoff (25,000 MWCO for NGF and 50,000 MWCO for Sema3A).
Place each protein sample in respective dialysis buffer 1 for 4 hr at 4°C.
Replace buffer with respective buffer 2 overnight at 4°C.
Concentrate the dialyzed protein elutions to less than 5 ml using centrifuge spin concentrators.
Determine protein concentration (mg/ml) by freeze drying a sample in a preweighed microcentrifuge tube.
Transfer recombinant proteins to 2 ml micro-centrifuge tubes for biotinylation.
Biotinylate proteins using a biotin protein ligase kit.
Dialyze proteins against PBS using 10,000 MWCO dialysis cassettes with 3 buffer changes a day for 2 days.
Determine the percent biotinylation of proteins using a quantitation kit.
Determine the concentration of the solution as described in 6.4.
Store the solution at 4°C or aliquot and store at -20°C for long-term storage.
